newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends higher.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends higher.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures rose above their mixed midsession levels and ended higher on commercial buying, spillover support from other markets and tightness in nearby stocks, traders said.

Brokers noted that the snow that has buried much of the northern U.S. Plains in the last week has paralyzed grain movement, making it difficult to originate wheat from the country and helping basis levels remain firm.
"We had strong commercial buying, spillover from beans and people covering their (short positions)," a trader said. "You've also got tightness in nearbys."
Spring wheat also drew support from CBOT and KCBT wheat, which firmed on weather concerns and lingering bullishness over Friday's USDA winter wheat seeding report.
MGE spring wheat closed 3-1/2 to 4-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up 4-3/4 cents at $3.93-1/2.
Traders said Atwood-Peavey was a featured player, buying one million March and 800,000 May bushels. CIS bought 600,000 March. LFG sold 1.4 million March on a spread with Chicago, traders said.
MGE barley futures did not trade and closed unchanged.
